_doc: HAND-AUTHORED. Forty cards of EACH volume read, drawn at random and adjudicated one by one against the rendered page image. Nothing else in this domain measures whether the reading is any good; this does, and it is the reason the README can put a number on it instead of an adjective. Schema 2 holds one block per volume, because a number drawn on volume 1 is not a measurement of volume 2 — the top-level counts are the flat total the gate checks, and `volumes` carries the figure that actually belongs to each reading.
generated_by: hand — the draw is reproducible, the verdicts are not
not_a_reading: a MEASUREMENT of this domain's reading, not a reading. Every one of these 160 rows re-adjudicates a card already read and already counted in records/, so charging them again would mean the domain read 160 more names by looking harder at the names it had. T-0602: tools/measure_research_spend.py withholds them from the read count and prints this sentence when it does.

draw.maintained: T-0600: the draw is MAINTAINED, not re-thrown. A rule change that strikes cards takes their rows out of this sample and replaces them, in the same stratum, with `random.seed(1835); random.sample([the stratum's cards not already sampled], n)` over records/entries_vol_01.json as it now stands. Sequential sampling without replacement is still a uniform sample of the cards that remain, and it keeps the hand adjudications that are still true instead of re-making every verdict to reach the same answers. Replaced in this pass: nbi_v01_1796, nbi_v01_2218, nbi_v01_2226, nbi_v01_0605 -> nbi_v01_0495, nbi_v01_1925, nbi_v01_0658, nbi_v01_2418.

found: One systematic false positive, now struck by a rule: the index carries thousands of English cards citing the Calendarium Inquisitionum by regnal year — 'Calendarium, Hen. III. and Edw. I' — and ', III.' is the shape of ', Ill.'. tools/read_newberry_index.py REGNAL refuses them, and 35 cards left the volume when it was added. The sample was redrawn afterwards and this file adjudicates the redrawn one.
One card this reading should not have kept: nbi_v01_2226, whose whole line is 'I II.'. It is kept, with its verdict, because a struck card nobody can see is a precision figure nobody can check.

Chicago antiquities (Hurlbut, 1881) and the Second Presbyterian Church register 1842-92 (Grant) both surfaced in the sample and neither is in this project's sources. The first is now in the follow-up table.

T-0600 STRUCK FOUR OF THESE FORTY, AND THREE OF THEM WERE GRADED CORRECT HERE. nbi_v01_2218 ('Draper | ILLINOIS', noted at the time as 'a locality divider card reading ILLINOIS'), nbi_v01_0605 ('Biabee | — Illinois. !1 *') and nbi_v01_1796 ('Crawford | Chicago,', 'and nothing else legible. Kept, because the locality is what is being recorded') are the class volume 2's draw diagnosed as the state banner; this volume's draw saw all three and let them stand. The rule reads the missing thing instead of the spelling: a card body is a CITATION, and a stanza that names the place and no work can never become a lead. nbi_v01_2226 ('I II.'), carried here as the volume's one bad keep, goes with them. 154 cards left volume 1, 19 of them Chicago-or-Cook.

found: THE STATE BANNER ABSORBED AS A CARD BODY — four of the five bad keeps, and a class volume 1's sample did not surface. The index divides a family's cards by state with a printed rule, 'ILLINOIS.'; when that rule falls directly under a heading, the extractor reads it as that card's body and keeps the stanza. nbi_v02_0561, nbi_v02_1675, nbi_v02_1027 and nbi_v02_0539 are the four in this draw, and nbi_v02_1675 is the proof the banner does not belong to the heading above it: the heading is 'Kinge or King family.', whose one card is an English parish register, and the surname run under the banner is KINGERY. All four are kept with their verdicts rather than struck, because a struck card nobody can see is a precision figure nobody can check; T-0600 carries the rule.

A CALL NUMBER READ AS A STATE — the fifth. nbi_v02_1106 is 'Holden family. — Hapgood fam. (Hapgood, W.) 1898. See index. E. 7. H 21', a family genealogy naming no locality; the ', III,' the illinois_abbreviated pattern matched on is the wreck of the Newberry call number. Unlike the banner it names nothing true, and it is the sharper half of T-0600.

THE CHICAGO AND COOK STRATUM IS 20 OF 20 — the cards that set the reading order in follow_up.json did not miss once in this draw, and every bad keep in the volume's sample is in the Illinois-only stratum. Volume 1's single figure of 0.975 could not show this because it did not report by stratum; the blocks here do, and volume 1's rows have been re-counted under the same split without a verdict being changed.

The draw is stratified 20/20 and the volume is not: 501 of the 1,987 kept cards are Chicago or Cook. Weighted by the population the estimate is 0.813, and the unstratified 0.875 above is the figure comparable with volume 1's.

A SLIVER IS A SECOND CARD. nbi_v02_1775 reads 'Krlog | Cook Co..' — the left edge of a card standing in column 3, caught by column 2's 200-point window, which column 3 also read in full as nbi_v02_1779. The passes are deduplicated on (page, heading, body) and a truncated sliver never matches its full sibling. Correct on locality, so it is not counted against precision, and it inflates the card count. T-0601 measures how many.

A CHICAGO CARD LOST TO THE BUCKET. nbi_v02_0937 is 'Henrotin family. — Chicago, Ill. (Andreas, A. T.) 1884-6', and the reading dropped the word 'Chicago' from the body, so it is bucketed illinois_abbreviated and is not among the 501. A recall loss, not a precision error — this sample cannot measure recall, and the 501 is a floor, not a count.

Two works surfaced in the draw that this project already holds and that the follow-up table ranks: the Fergus Historical Series' 1839 Chicago directory (cards under Foster and Graves, both immediately beneath their Andreas card) and the Second Presbyterian Church register 1842-92.

T-0600 STRUCK SIX OF THESE FORTY: the four banners (nbi_v02_0561, nbi_v02_1675, nbi_v02_1027, nbi_v02_0539), the call number read as a state (nbi_v02_1106), and — as a side effect of the same rule, its body being 'Cook Co..' and nothing more — the sliver nbi_v02_1775 that T-0601 counts. 101 cards left volume 2, 9 of them Chicago-or-Cook. The six replacements were adjudicated against the page image the same way, and one of them (nbi_v02_0610) is a sliver of a shape these rules do not catch, so the volume still carries one bad keep in forty: 0.875 -> 0.975.

found: THE COLUMN SLIVER SUPPLIES A LOCALITY THE CARD DOES NOT HAVE — one bad keep (nbi_v03_0913) and, on a card that is otherwise a good keep, one wrong surname (nbi_v03_1154 is filed under the neighbour's 'Onslow'). The crop boxes are 200 points wide on a 173-point pitch, deliberately, so a column always arrives whole; the cost is a sliver of the next column on every page, and where the sliver's first word is 'Illinois' or its heading is nearer the line than the card's own, the assembled card is a hybrid of two columns. Deduplication on (page, heading, body) does not catch it, because the hybrid is not a duplicate of anything. Both are left in the volume, with their verdicts, rather than struck: a card nobody can see is a precision figure nobody can check (volume 1's rule).

'SEE INDEX III.' IS A VOLUME NUMBER — nbi_v03_1443, and it is the class this volume adds. The cards cite a genealogy's index volume in roman, and ', III.' after a stop is the shape the illinois_abbreviated pattern is looking for. It is the regnal problem in a second dress, and it is commoner: two of the four cards in that one rendered window carry the formula.

THE REGNAL RULE PASSES A CARD IT WAS WRITTEN TO STOP — nbi_v03_0653, 'Calendarium, Hen. III. and Edw. I', read by the OCR as 'Calendafium, Han, iii. and i n .'. REGNAL matches the regnal name and a capitalised numeral; here neither survived the photostat. Volume 1 struck 35 cards with that rule and this volume shows what it still lets through.

A PRINTED BANNER IS NOT THE ONLY WAY A NON-ILLINOIS CARD IS KEPT — nbi_v03_1870 is a NEW ENGLAND card whose reading opens 'lil.', which is on no card; the illinois_abbreviated pattern anchors on start-of-line as well as on a comma, and a mark left by the rule above the card satisfies it. Volume 2's banner class and this are the same failure at two different sources.

WIDE PAGES TRUNCATE COLUMN 3's HEADINGS — nbi_v03_0849 is filed under 'rtenoan' because page 375's printed column 3 begins left of the 519-point crop. The card's locality is right and its surname key is not, so it can never join a lead. The crop comment already records that page widths run 689 to 733 points; this is what the widest of them costs.

Nothing in the forty was a Chicago or Cook card that should not have been kept: 20 of 20, as in volumes 1 and 2. Every bad keep in three volumes has been an Illinois-only one, and every one of them has come from text that is not on the card.

T-0600 STRUCK ONE OF THESE FORTY — nbi_v03_0913, the sliver that supplied a locality the card did not have, already graded not_demonstrated here. 127 cards left volume 3, 18 of them Chicago-or-Cook. This volume's draw was not re-thrown for it; the row was replaced from the same stratum and adjudicated against the page image. 0.900 -> 0.925.

The strata are therefore not the same sizes as volumes 1-3 and the two per-stratum figures below are what to compare, not the flat one.

found: THE VOLUME'S TEXT LAYER IS A DIFFERENT AND MUCH WORSE SCAN, and it is the whole story of this block. 6,548 cards were assembled from 918 pages — 7 a page, against 59, 58 and 68 a page in volumes 1, 2 and 3. A rendered page carries about 100 cards, so the earlier volumes assembled roughly 60 per cent of what is printed and this one assembles seven. 308 cards were kept against 2,579, 1,987 and 2,131; ten of them name Chicago or Cook County, against 581, 501 and 520. The card that reads 'Stoddard family.' on the page comes back from this volume's text layer as "s:'o'ddnrdmany.", and the heading rule needs the family word as its own token. Volume 4 is also the one file in the Internet Archive item without the Newberry's scan id — '130151_04.pdf' beside 'FL2091539_CP-130151_01.pdf' and its two fellows — so a different digitisation is the likely cause. T-0613 carries the repair.

THE CROP GEOMETRY WAS TESTED AND RULED OUT, so the shortfall could not be blamed on this project's reading. The gutters of volume 4 were measured over sixty pages from every word box on them: they fall at 192, 348 and 508 points, and the shared 200-point windows on a 173-point pitch contain each column whole. Boxes cut to the measured gutters moved heading detection from 576 to 616 over the same 61 pages — 7 per cent, against an eight-fold shortfall. The shared boxes were therefore KEPT, and volume 4 is read by exactly the method volumes 1-3 were, which is what makes the comparison above mean anything.

THE COLLAPSE IS ENTIRELY IN THE ILLINOIS-ONLY STRATUM. Chicago-and-Cook scores 0.900 — one bad keep in ten, the column sliver — which is volume 2's and volume 3's number, and it is the stratum the follow-up table and the acquisition list stand on. Illinois-only scores 0.333: twenty bad keeps in thirty. Six classes, and only one of them is new. Already named: the column sliver (nbi_v04_0174, 0190), 'See Index III.' as a genealogy's index volume (0223, 0275), the state banner or a bare 'Illinois' that is not the card's own line (0219, 0125), and the body that is nothing but mush (0205, 0290, 0228, 0211, 0057, 0170). NEW HERE: a PAGE NUMBER read as the abbreviation — nbi_v04_0183 is 'Woodruff fam. (Woodruff, F.E.) 1902:117' and the '117' came back as '111,'. The anchor the pattern already carries (a comma or a line start before the strokes) does not catch it, because the OCR supplies the comma.

AND THE TEN CHICAGO CARDS ARE THEMSELVES AN UNDERCOUNT. Three of the ten good keeps in the illinois-only stratum are Chicago cards the chicago pattern missed — 'Chicngo' (nbi_v04_0173), 'Gkgo' (0188) and 'Chh:|go' (0126) — none of which the pattern will take, because it demands i, l or 1 in the second and third places. Three in thirty sampled, on 298 illinois-only cards, puts the true Chicago-or-Cook figure nearer thirty than ten. The pattern is not widened to chase them: at this text quality a wider one would take page numbers as well, and T-0613's re-read is the answer that does not cost precision.

T-0600 STRUCK EIGHT OF THESE FORTY, seven of them already graded not_demonstrated here — the bare 'Illinois', the bare 'Iii.', 'I 11 .', 'III. 1.' and their kind, which is most of what made this volume's 0.475. 61 cards left volume 4, 1 of them Chicago-or-Cook, and that one is the eighth: nbi_v04_0094, 'Staalrmn | *5 ._.ChicAgo, m. <.-...«..-.5.', graded locality_correct because the card really is 'Steen family. — Chicago, Ill. (Andreas, A. T.) 1884-6'. Its READING names no work, which is what the rule tests, so it goes with the rest — a recall loss this sample can see and name, and the reason the Chicago-or-Cook stratum here is now a census of 9 rather than 10 and the volume's sample is 39. 0.475 -> 0.513. Volume 4 is still the worst reading in the domain by a wide margin, and the seven new rows say why: an author's initials, a wrecked Massachusetts card, a France card and a New Hampshire run all still match the abbreviation.
